aboutParagraphs: Cedar Hill Park in Madison is Nashville's quiet heavyweight — a 21-hole course with quite varied terrain that threads a 3-hole inner loop between holes 2 and 3, giving the round an unusual rhythm. From the standard tees it plays 6,828 feet at par 68.
Free to play and very cart friendly, with concrete tees and DISCatcher baskets. The baskets move regularly, so the course stays fresh even for regulars — every visit can play a little differently.
It's less famous than Seven Oaks but just as loved by the locals who prefer a longer, more varied walk in the woods.

signatureHoleDescription: Hole 21 closes Cedar Hill at 570 feet — a par 4 that ends the 21-hole loop the way it started: long, fair, and full of variety. The inner-loop rhythm of the course makes this final stretch feel earned, and the finish is one of the most satisfying in Nashville's stable of park courses.
localTips: The course is 21 holes with a 3-hole inner loop between holes 2 and 3 — on the course signs the loop holes are labeled I1–I3. Baskets move regularly, so check the current layout. Free to play and very cart friendly.
